# UNM Center for Advanced Research Computing

> The UNM Center for Advanced Research Computing (CARC): mission, research, the CSE certificate program, news, and contact information. User documentation for CARC systems lives at https://carc.unm.edu/docs/ (with its own llms.txt). The source repository is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) bundle: every page carries YAML frontmatter with type, provenance, and lifecycle fields.

Full corpus for ingestion: https://carc.unm.edu/llms-full.txt

Every page's Markdown source (OKF frontmatter included) is served at its URL plus `index.md` — for example https://carc.unm.edu/about/mission/index.md. Agent guide: https://carc.unm.edu/docs/about/ai-agents/

## About CARC

- [History](https://carc.unm.edu/about/history/): A timeline of CARC milestones from the founding of the Maui and Albuquerque high performance computing centers in the 1990s through recent system donations and retirements.
- [Internal Advisory Board](https://carc.unm.edu/about/iab/): Membership roster and meeting minutes of the CARC Internal Advisory Board, which meets regularly to make decisions regarding the center's operations and goals.
- [Mission and vision](https://carc.unm.edu/about/mission/): CARC's vision and mission: leading and growing the computational research community at UNM.
- [Strategic plan](https://carc.unm.edu/about/strategic-plan/): An overview of CARC's strategic plan to meet user needs and develop a sustainable funding model, with a link to the full plan PDF.

## Research

- [Featured projects](https://carc.unm.edu/research/featured-projects/): Feature articles highlighting research projects done using computing, storage, and support resources at the Center for Advanced Research Computing.
- [Free research computing](https://carc.unm.edu/research/free-services/): A description of the free baseline research computing service CARC provides to UNM main campus users, including the core-hour and storage limits.
- [Grant writing resources](https://carc.unm.edu/research/grant-resources/): Links to UNM training, funding search, proposal development, compliance, and submission resources for researchers writing grant proposals.
- [Premium services](https://carc.unm.edu/research/premium-services/): CARC's UNM-approved cost model for condo cluster nodes, VM hosting, dedicated storage, and custom support for users whose needs exceed the free baseline service.
- [Publications and acknowledgement](https://carc.unm.edu/research/publications/): The acknowledgement statement to use in publications that made use of CARC resources, and a link to view publications that feature the center.

## Education & training

- [Workshops and seminars](https://carc.unm.edu/education/workshops/): Free CARC workshops in the 1601 Central workshop room, the live events calendar, and video alternatives.

## CSE Certificate Program

- [CSE application](https://carc.unm.edu/education/cse/application/): How to apply to the CSE Certificate Program through the UNM ApplyYourself portal.
- [Electives and participating departments](https://carc.unm.edu/education/cse/electives/): Approved CSE elective courses by department — with live schedule links and Fall 2026 offering status — and the departments participating in the certificate program.
- [CSE program requirements](https://carc.unm.edu/education/cse/requirements/): Admission prerequisites, core courses, elective hours, and the research project requirement for the CSE certificate.
- [Program specializations](https://carc.unm.edu/education/cse/specializations/): Optional, non-transcripted CSE specializations: Computational Fluid Dynamics and Data Science.

## News

- [Registration is open for the 2025 CARC Annual Meeting (CAM)](https://carc.unm.edu/news/2025-annual-meeting/): CARC's fourth annual user meeting — April 14, 2025 — with a keynote, open forum, and student poster session.
- [Registration is open for the 2026 CARC Annual Meeting](https://carc.unm.edu/news/2026-annual-meeting/): CAM 2026 comes to Zimmerman Library B30 on April 21, 2026 — updates, research highlights, and the student poster session.
- [Remembering Cleve Moler](https://carc.unm.edu/news/cleve-moler-memoriam/): Matthew Fricke remembers Cleve Moler — creator of MATLAB, former UNM Computer Science chair, and a giant of high-performance computing — who died on May 20, 2026, at 86.
- [Recent departures and retirements](https://carc.unm.edu/news/departures-retirements/): Thanking Patrick Bridges and Hussein Al-Azzawi, and wishing Jim Prewett a happy retirement. (draft)
- [An important message from our Director](https://carc.unm.edu/news/director-message/): A message to the CARC community from then-Director Patrick G. Bridges on federal executive actions and CARC's commitments.
- [UNM launches search for the next director of CARC](https://carc.unm.edu/news/director-search/): The University seeks a strategic and operational leader for the Center for Advanced Research Computing. This search has concluded.
- [CARC prepares for deployment of new high-performance computing cluster](https://carc.unm.edu/news/easley-cluster/): Easley — named for NASA pioneer Annie Easley — brings H100 GPUs, all-flash storage, and a 7–10× performance leap.
- [Genome sequencing reveals a newly identified virus](https://carc.unm.edu/news/genome-sequencing/): CARC computing supported the sequencing and phylogenetic analysis behind the characterization of a previously unrecognized virus.
- [New HPC course bridges the gap between students and local tech industry](https://carc.unm.edu/news/hpc-course/): CS491/591, led by Matthew Fricke and backed by a $1M Department of Education grant, gives students hands-on cluster experience.
- [Undergraduate researcher leverages CARC for molecular modeling breakthrough](https://carc.unm.edu/news/molecular-modeling/): Physics major Sole Samuels used CARC systems to develop radial density encoding, a new molecular representation for machine learning.
- [New NSF research hardware award](https://carc.unm.edu/news/nsf-hardware-ruskai/): A new NSF award led by Ruskai brings new research computing hardware to UNM. (draft)
- [New NSF award: IDSS MESA](https://carc.unm.edu/news/nsf-idss-mesa/): A new National Science Foundation award supports the IDSS MESA project. (draft)
- [PSAAP COMPASS center: 2026 update](https://carc.unm.edu/news/psaap-2026-update/): An update on the DOE NNSA PSAAP IV COMPASS center led by UNM. (draft)
- [UNM awarded prestigious grant to lead national research on high-performance computing](https://carc.unm.edu/news/psaap-iv-compass/): A UNM-led team wins a DOE NNSA PSAAP IV cooperative agreement, establishing the COMPASS center at CARC.
- [CARC team gears up for SC24 Competition](https://carc.unm.edu/news/sc24-team/): Six UNM students take a Dell/Penguin/Intersect360-sponsored H100 cluster to the SC24 student competition in Atlanta.
- [Welcome our new CARC Director, Tyson Swetnam](https://carc.unm.edu/news/welcome-director-swetnam/): The Center for Advanced Research Computing welcomes Tyson Swetnam as its new Director. (draft)

## Contact

- [Personnel](https://carc.unm.edu/contact/personnel/): The CARC team: leadership, systems staff, and administration.
- [Visiting CARC](https://carc.unm.edu/contact/visiting/): Location, directions, and parking for the CARC building at 1601 Central Avenue NE.
